item.title: Demystifying macOS Platform SSO: How Apple and Microsoft Entra ID work together
item.description:
Platform SSO has been transforming the macOS sign-in experience by bringing Microsoft Entra authentication closer to the operating system. Users can sign in to their Mac and access work applications with fewer authentication prompts, while organizations retain Microsoft Entra device trust and access controls.

As more organizations deploy Platform SSO, new questions have emerged:

  • What actually happens under the hood?
  • Which responsibilities belong to Apple, and which belong to Microsoft?
  • Where are credentials created and protected?
  • Does every application receive the Platform SSO Primary Refresh Token (PRT)?

To help answer these questions, we published a new Microsoft Learn article: Architecture and authentication flow for macOS Platform SSO with Microsoft Entra ID.

Apple Platform SSO is an extensible framework that can work with supported identity-provider extensions. This post focuses on its integration with Microsoft Entra ID through the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in. It provides a practical mental model, highlights the ownership boundaries between Apple and Microsoft, and walks through the key parts of the architecture.

Why the ownership boundary can be difficult to see

From the user's perspective, Platform SSO can feel like one continuous experience. The Mac is enrolled, the user completes registration, and supported applications begin signing in with fewer prompts.

Behind that experience, however, several systems retain distinct responsibilities. MDM (Mobile Device Management) deploys the Platform SSO policy. The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in connects the Mac to Microsoft Entra ID. macOS owns the operating-system experience and protects the platform credentials. Microsoft Entra ID validates the authentication proofs and issues identity credentials. Applications consume only the authorization intended for them.

Platform SSO is a shared architecture across device management, Apple, and Microsoft. The following diagram shows how responsibilities are divided across the end-to-end flow.

Ownership boundaries in macOS Platform SSO with Microsoft Entra ID.

This division of responsibility isn't just an implementation detail. It establishes the security boundaries that allow Platform SSO to reduce authentication prompts without distributing powerful credentials to every application.

Three ideas that make the architecture easier to understand

1. Registration and SSO aren't the same operation

Registration establishes trust. It connects the managed Mac and local user to Microsoft Entra ID, registers the required public-key material, and gives macOS the identity-provider configuration it needs for later authentication.

SSO begins when macOS uses that established trust to obtain and protect the Platform SSO PRT.

Separating these concepts answers many common questions: a registered device doesn't mean every application has already received a token. Registration creates the foundation that allows macOS and the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in to perform supported SSO operations later.

2. The Platform SSO PRT belongs to the Platform SSO architecture—not to applications

Applications don’t receive the Platform SSO PRT, device private keys, or the user's authentication private key. macOS protects the Platform SSO PRT and makes it available to the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in through Apple's supported Platform SSO framework. When an application needs access to a resource, the plug-in uses the PRT as part of the Microsoft Entra authorization flow. The application receives only the token or session issued for its own client and target resource.

This distinction is important: Platform SSO provides a shared sign-in experience without turning the PRT into a shared application credential.

3. Authentication methods change the proof—not the overall architecture

Organizations can configure Password, UserSecureEnclaveKey, or SmartCard as the authentication method. Each method changes how the user proves their identity:

  • Password uses the user's Microsoft Entra credential and can keep the local macOS password synchronized.
  • UserSecureEnclaveKey uses a hardware-bound key protected by the Secure Enclave.
  • SmartCard uses a certificate and its associated private key.

The broader architecture remains the same. macOS obtains the configured user proof, binds the request to the registered Mac, and sends the request to Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft Entra ID verifies the registered credential and validates the user and device proofs before issuing the Platform SSO PRT.

As a result, choosing an authentication method is primarily a decision about user experience, credential protection, and organizational security requirements—not a completely different SSO architecture.

What this means for customers

Understanding the ownership boundaries helps administrators reason about deployment and troubleshooting:

  • MDM configuration starts the experience. Platform SSO behavior depends on the policy delivered to the Mac.
  • Apple owns the native operating-system integration. macOS controls the sign-in experience and protects the platform credentials.
  • Microsoft connects the Mac to Microsoft Entra ID through the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in. The plug-in performs registration and participates in supported SSO flows.
  • Microsoft Entra ID remains the token-issuing authority. It validates the registered device and the authentication result—including proof from a federated identity provider when applicable—and issues the Platform SSO PRT and subsequent Microsoft Entra tokens.
  • Applications remain isolated. They receive authorization for their own resources rather than direct access to the Platform SSO PRT.

The result is an architecture that combines a native macOS experience with Microsoft Entra device identity, application isolation, and hardware-backed authentication options.

Common misconceptions

"UserSecureEnclaveKey means a password is never needed"

UserSecureEnclaveKey provides passwordless authentication to Microsoft Entra ID, but it doesn't remove every macOS password requirement. FileVault and the startup sequence retain their own requirements, and users generally need the local account password for the first unlock after a restart.

"The registration certificate is the user's credential"

The registration certificate represents the registered device’s signing key. It helps Microsoft Entra ID identify and validate the registered Mac. The user's identity is proved separately through Password, UserSecureEnclaveKey, or SmartCard authentication.

"Applications receive the Platform SSO PRT"

Applications receive tokens or sessions issued for their own client and target resources. macOS protects the Platform SSO PRT and exposes it only to the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in through Apple's supported Platform SSO framework.

"The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in provides Kerberos SSO by itself"

Kerberos SSO is another example of shared ownership. Microsoft Entra ID can return cloud and on-premises Kerberos ticket-granting tickets (TGTs) alongside the PRT in the same protected Platform SSO response. The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in supplies the ticket mappings that tell macOS which TGTs to import. macOS Platform SSO validates the response and imports the selected TGTs into a Kerberos credential cache.

If the Kerberos SSO extension is configured to use Platform SSO TGTs, it consumes a matching TGT from macOS and obtains service tickets for supported cloud or on-premises resources. The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in, macOS Platform SSO, and the Kerberos SSO extension therefore have separate roles; no single component owns the complete Kerberos SSO flow.

Explore the complete architecture

This post intentionally focuses on the mental model and ownership boundaries. The Microsoft Learn architecture page provides the maintained technical reference, including:

  • Device and user registration
  • Platform SSO PRT acquisition and refresh
  • Password, UserSecureEnclaveKey, and SmartCard authentication
  • Cloud and on-premises Kerberos TGTs
  • Platform Credential passkeys
  • Detailed architecture and sequence diagrams

For the complete technical flows and diagrams, see Architecture and authentication flow for macOS Platform SSO with Microsoft Entra ID.

-Veena Soman

Principal Software Engineer, Microsoft | LinkedIn

item.title: AI is changing access. See how Microsoft Entra helps you stay ahead.
item.description:
⭐Don't miss Microsoft Ignite BRK343 to see demos of what's in this post.⭐

Wednesday, November 18, 2026, 10:15 to 11:00 AM Pacific Time

Watch: AI is changing access. See how Microsoft Entra helps you stay ahead.

AI and agents are changing the access landscape at a pace that challenges even mature identity and security programs. Without centralized visibility and control, agent sprawl risks becoming shadow IT at a scale we've never had to manage before.

AI amplifies today's identity challenges. Every agent needs an identity, the right access, and controls that adapt as risk changes.
We're designing Microsoft Entra for this reality: secure access for every identity, human or agent, to every resource, from anywhere.

This week at Microsoft Ignite, we're announcing new Microsoft Entra capabilities, advancing this strategy around three customer priorities: strengthen your identity foundation, secure agent access at scale, and turn customer identity into a competitive advantage.

Strengthen your identity foundation

Agent adoption makes strengthening the identity foundation more urgent.
Agents inherit unnecessary privileges, persistent access, and weak governance. Today's identity backlog becomes tomorrow's agent security problem.

As one practitioner told us, “If you're not doing it for humans today, you're going to struggle with agents.”

Make every sign-in phishing-resistant and verified

Secure access starts with phishing-resistant credentials like passkeys, now the default for new accounts in Microsoft Entra. Yet 57% of organizations still rely on phishable authentication methods.[i] Weaker credentials like SMS codes leave users vulnerable to adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing attacks, which target not only sign-ins, but also onboarding and account recovery.

  • High assurance credentials (preview). A strong credential is only as trustworthy as the process used to issue and recover it. You can now combine passkeys with trusted identity verification throughout the credential lifecycle, including when someone onboards and first gets a passkey, before they access a sensitive resource or join a sensitive meeting, and when they recover their account. Microsoft Entra supports identity verification from partners including AU10TIX, IDEMIA, CLEAR, 1Kosmos, Entrust, Persona, and TrueCredential. Learn more.
  • Secure enterprise browser for BYOD with Microsoft Edge for Business and Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access (preview). Legacy VPNs give users access that’s too broad. With Microsoft Entra Global Secure access, users simply sign in to their Microsoft Edge work profile, even on a personal device, to gain secure access to your private apps. The Secure Web and AI gateway protects their browsing activity. Learn more.  

Reduce standing access and policy sprawl

Attackers exploit standing access and inconsistent policies. Just-in-time privileges and consistent controls reduce how far they can move.
  • Expanded privileged access controls in Privileged Identity Management (preview). Privileged access should be temporary, monitored, and limited to the task at hand. We’ve extended just-in-time access to more users, resources, and AI agents. Users can activate roles and connect to Azure and Azure Arc virtual machines from the My Access portal, while admins can monitor privileged sessions, manage them, and review session recordings. For the task at hand, users get AI-based recommendations for least-privileged roles. Additional features extend PIM to application roles and AI agents, add PIM-only mode to enforce role assignment policies, and introduce bulk management to reduce standing access at scale. Learn more.
  • Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans (preview). Instead of configuring the same requirement multiple times, you can now design your policy intent once and enforce it everywhere it applies, for every identity. Define shared assignments, resources, and conditions at the plan level, then add individual access requirements as rules, so you can build comprehensive policies without gaps or conflicts. Templates, including ones for AI agents, provide shortcuts to a stronger security posture. Learn more.
  • Advanced capabilities for Microsoft Entra dynamic membership groups (preview). Organizational change can leave access and governance groups out of sync. New dynamic membership capabilities in Microsoft Entra ID Governance reduce manual maintenance by automatically aligning groups with existing memberships and reporting structures. MemberOf Next brings together membership from selected groups, while Transitive Reports To extends membership across an entire reporting hierarchy. Learn more.
  • Microsoft Entra ID Governance Guest lifecycle policies (generally available). Inactive or unnecessary guest accounts can become attack vectors. Instead of relying on manual cleanup, you can automate governance across the full guest lifecycle with policies that continuously evaluate sponsorship, inactivity, and invitation status and that define what happens when a guest no longer meets requirements. Built-in reporting shows which guests each policy affects before and during enforcement, while sponsors can view and act on the guests they support. Learn more.

Govern every tenant and minimize disruptions

Most large organizations run many tenants. When Central IT doesn't know about some shadow tenants, they can't easily verify that each is configured securely. Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance gives you a unified way to find every tenant, bring it under governance, and detect configuration drift across identity, security, and productivity workloads.

  • Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance cross-tenant configuration management and Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview). You can now deploy, monitor, and enforce resource configurations and detect drift across all your tenants from a single pane of glass. Learn more.
  • Multitenant management for Microsoft Agent 365 and Copilot (preview). You can also extend Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance to Agent 365 and Copilot. This helps you manage agents and AI at scale and maintain consistent configurations across your estate. Learn more.

One accidental change or security compromise can leave critical identity settings broken or exposed, disrupting access across your organization. Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery automatically backs up critical identity data, from agent identities to Conditional Access policies, so you can restore them to a known good state and minimize disruption.

  • Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery Premium (preview). Premium extends retention to 30 days and integrates with Microsoft 365 Backup for comprehensive resilience across identity and productivity data. Learn more.
  • Microsoft Entra hard deletion protection (preview). You can protect crucial tenant objects such as Agent IDs from permanent deletion. Learn more.

Put AI to work on everyday administration

AI can reduce repetitive administration so teams can focus on higher-value security decisions.
  • Microsoft MCP Server for IT Admins (generally available). AI tools and agents are useful for automating repetitive, time-consuming tasks. Now you can connect them to data and intelligence in Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, and Microsoft Intune to answer queries and help with complex tasks. Learn more.

See it in BRK343: Watch Nichole require a high assurance credential before an attendee can join a Teams meeting, build a Conditional Access policy plan in minutes, use PIM for just-in-time sign-in to a Linux VM with session recording, and enable single sign-on for a new enterprise app from an AI assistant connected to Microsoft MCP Server for IT Admins. Watch it live or as a replay.

Secure agent access

Organizations everywhere are adopting AI agents to boost innovation and productivity. Industry projections estimate roughly 1.3 billion agents in production by 2028, running on any cloud, as SaaS apps, or locally on employee devices. But what agents are operating in your environment? Which resources can each one access? And how do you stop one—right now?

Find every agent and give it an identity

Securing agents starts with finding them, giving each one an identity, and registering it so you can govern its access.
  • Microsoft Entra Agent ID for discovered local agents (preview). With Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access, you can discover 60 local agent types, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI. Each discovered agent receives an Agent ID, so you can govern and protect its access. Learn more.
  • Microsoft Entra Agent ID for digital teammates (preview). Expanded support for Microsoft agent platforms now includes digital teammates, which get their own agent user account and ID. Apply Conditional Access, ID Protection, and access governance to the work a digital teammate does under its own identity, separate from the identity of the human user it’s working for. Learn more.

Govern agent access across its lifecycle

Agents need least-privileged access that's reviewed and removed when no longer needed. Because agents will outnumber people, lifecycle governance must be automated.
  • ID Governance Dynamic permissions for permission remediation (preview). You can discover agent identities with excessive privileges in the connected business application, then investigate those privileges alongside our recommended remediation and remediate them to ensure governance of agentic access at scale. Learn more.
  • Automated lifecycle management of agent identities (generally available). You can now configure lifecycle policies for agents. They check whether each agent has a human sponsor, is still needed, and has been active recently. If not, Microsoft Entra sends notifications and later disables or deletes the agent according to your instructions. An out-of-the-box policy disables agent identities that have been inactive for 60 days. Learn more.
  • Access packages for digital teammates (preview). Access packages for Microsoft and third-party cloud agents are already available. Now you can also assign access packages to digital teammates, with approval and time-limit policies. Learn more.

Adapt agent access to risk in real time

If a person's sign-in looks risky, Conditional Access can block them, limit access, or require additional verification. Agents need the same ability to respond to changing risk, without unnecessarily disrupting the people working alongside them. In Microsoft telemetry on Azure AI workloads, tool and agent abuse accounted for 12% of observed attack activity.

  • Dynamic Agent Risk (Agent 365 preview). Dynamic Agent Risk combines signals from identity, data, endpoints, cloud, network, runtime, and the agent's own activity, such as whether an agent runs in a container or loose in the operating system, and whether the data it's trying to reach is sensitive. It continuously updates each agent's risk score using signals from Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Defender, and Microsoft Purview (with more to come) so that access adjusts accordingly.
  • Conditional Access policies for assistive agents (preview). Conditional Access can now distinguish between people and local agents acting on their behalf, so separate policies can, for example, block a high-risk agent while the employee keeps working. A new actions and destinations option extends protection from applications to individual sensitive operations, so you can restrict sensitive actions during risky sessions while routine work continues. Learn more.
  • Conditional Access support for Windows 365 for Agents (generally available). Conditional Access now extends to the Cloud PCs your agents use. Learn more.
We're also extending network visibility and controls to agent traffic.
  • Agentic traffic acquisition in Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access (preview). You can acquire agentic traffic to gain visibility and network controls specifically for agents while preserving your SASE solution and existing security architecture. Learn more.
  • Agent type-aware network controls for local agents (preview). With network policies tailored to specific local agents running on employee devices, you gain greater visibility and control over how individual agents access network resources and destinations. Learn more.  
  • MCP firewall (preview). For granular control over agent-to-MCP communications, you can enforce policies across MCP servers, tools, resources, methods, protocol versions, and connection security requirements. Learn more.
  • Data security over the network with Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access (generally available). To protect sensitive data across human and on-behalf-of (OBO) agentic traffic, you can apply DLP policies at the network layer, including to unsanctioned AI apps. Learn more.

See it in BRK343: Watch Nichole bring agents from multiple AI platforms into a central inventory, view local agents discovered by Defender and Global Secure Access with their own agent identities, set up a lifecycle workflow that retires inactive agents, create an access package for digital teammates, restrict sensitive actions for assistive agents during risky sessions, and create an MCP policy that lets Claude Code and Claude Desktop use only trusted servers and tools. Watch it live or as a replay.

Also check out BRK339: Local agents are here. Can you find and secure them? for a deep dive on securing local agents, and LTG1242: AI agents need access. Your network needs controls (in person only) for a closer look at network controls for AI agent access.

Turn customer identity into a competitive advantage

Identity is the front door to your digital business. Microsoft Entra External ID helps make every customer interaction secure, simple, and on-brand, without requiring you to build identity infrastructure.

"As a frontier organization, we needed a modern and trustworthy identity and access experience for our 4 million customers. We chose Microsoft Entra External ID because it gave us a secure, scalable platform that is simple for our customers to use and lets us deliver a seamless, branded experience, so we can focus on serving people rather than managing identity infrastructure."

                                                                                                                        Alexander Kuthan, Project Manager, ASFINAG

New External ID capabilities give developers more control over authentication experiences while strengthening security.

Design branded, flexible sign-in experiences

Build differentiated sign-in experiences without building the underlying authentication system.
  • Customization with HTML templates and JavaScript support (preview). You can use your own HTML templates to build branded sign-up and sign-in experiences, with JavaScript for dynamic content that adapts to each step. This is rolling out now, with full availability by December 7. Learn more.
  • Bring your own UX authentication (preview). You can deliver differentiated experiences with fully customized, self-hosted authentication pages. External ID enforces authentication and access controls and manages single sign-on for you.
  • Sign-in with multiple first-factor methods (preview). You can support customers signing in with any of their first-factor methods, such as a passkey, one-time passcode, or email address and password.

Help developers move faster

  • Native Authentication API version 2 and SDKs (preview). A simpler integration experience, built to deliver new External ID features as soon as they're available, lets you embed authentication directly into mobile and single-page apps.
  • External ID AI agent toolkit (preview). With out-of-the-box skills, you can onboard an existing application to External ID by analyzing its code base or migrate native apps from version 1 to version 2 of the Native Authentication API.

Strengthen customer account security

  • Self-service credential management APIs (preview). You can now add self-service passkey registration and password updates to customer-facing apps through low-privilege delegated permissions, with email and phone management APIs coming soon. Learn more.
  • Time-based one-time passcodes for external users (preview). You can also offer a standards-based second factor for MFA in external tenants, with verification codes from Microsoft Authenticator or a supported third-party authenticator app. Learn more.

See it at Ignite: Catch the lightning talk about Microsoft Entra External ID: LTG1235, Customers Expect a Frictionless Login. Attackers Do Too (in person only) on Thursday, November 19, from 2:35 to 2:50 PM PT.

Catch us at Ignite and beyond

Join me, John Savill, and Nichole Peterson for BRK343 on Wednesday, November 18, at 10:15 AM PT to see these announcements in action.

Check in at a Microsoft Entra breakout session in person or online for a chance to win an Xbox plus a 30-minute chat with a Microsoft Entra identity architect. Official rules and eligibility requirements apply. Get the full Microsoft Entra schedule and prize draw details in Catch Microsoft Entra at Ignite 2026.  

AI is changing who and what needs access, and how quickly risk changes. Our goal is simple: give every identity the right access at the right time, with the visibility and control necessary to keep it that way.
Join us at Ignite, try these capabilities, and tell us what you need next.

Onwards,

Yina Arenas
Corporate Vice President and Chief Product Officer, Microsoft Identity and Network Access
Follow me on LinkedIn

 

⭐Want to go deeper after Ignite? ⭐

Post your questions now for our live AMA, Ask Microsoft Entra anything, on December 2, and join our Microsoft Entra webinar series from December 15 to 17 for more demos and practical guidance.

 

[i] The State of Passkeys 2026: Global Consumer and Workforce Report, FIDO Alliance, 2026.

item.title: What’s new in Microsoft Entra: November 2026
item.description:
Don't miss our Microsoft Ignite announcements. Tune in or join us in person for AI is changing access: See how Microsoft Entra helps you stay ahead on November 18, 2026, at 10:15 AM Pacific for secure access news and demos from our latest product roadmap.

Access is never a one-time decision. Employees change roles, devices fall out of compliance, AI agents get created and forgotten, and guests outlast the projects they joined for. But it’s not just identities that change: risks shift in real time and attacks never let up. Customers tell us the hardest part is keeping access secure as users, devices, agents, and guests change over time while threats evolve by the minute.

This month’s releases help you stay ahead of both: lifecycle policies for agent and guest identities, drift detection and group discovery for governed access, continuous access evaluation that responds to device and user risk signals within minutes, and phishing-resistant sign-in from the very first MFA method.

Here’s everything new in Microsoft Entra from October 2026, organized around the outcomes you’re trying to achieve:

Outcome: Keep my organization trusted and resilient

Detect drift in access package entitlements | Public Preview
Access package drift reports help you spot where real-world access diverges from policy intent. Flag over‑granted permissions or missing assignments and restore alignment with a click. Reports refresh daily and require Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite.
Learn more →

Discover and govern application groups | Public Preview
Account discovery now extends to groups. Find groups created directly within connected apps and bring them under governance. Classify them as local, unassigned, or assigned to streamline administration.
Learn more →

Outcome: Give users and agents secure access without friction

Apply a cloud firewall for Global Secure Access clients | Public Preview
Cloud firewall in Microsoft Entra Internet Access now covers Global Secure Access client traffic, allowing granular control over outbound network connections through rule‑based security profiles.
Learn more →

Support home network users reaching private access resources | Public Preview
Home network support ensures users can reach resources (printers, routers, displays) on their local network without disconnecting from Global Secure Access. The Prefer Local Network feature routes overlapping traffic directly to home devices.
Learn more →

Automate guest lifecycle policies for stronger security posture | Public Preview
Define guest policies based on sponsor attestation, recent activity, or redemption state. Automatically disable or delete guests who no longer meet requirements, reducing stale external access.
Learn more →

Register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as the first MFA method | General Availability
Users can now start with phishing-resistant authentication from day one—registering a passkey or passwordless option as their first MFA method. Rollout continues through February 2027.
Learn more →

Use Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors | General Availability
These device-bound credentials now qualify as standalone MFA factors across step-up prompts, Authentication Strength, and sign-in frequency checks—no additional passkey required. Rollout begins early November 2026.
Learn more →

Improve backup and restore for Microsoft Authenticator on Android | General Availability
New guidance simplifies secure backup of passkeys. Requires Google One backup and screen lock; applies only to personal profiles. Rollout begins January 2027.
Learn more →

Inform Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) with device and risk signals | General Availability
Universal CAE now evaluates both user and device risk. When a device is disabled or found noncompliant—or if high user risk is detected—the Global Secure Access client triggers reauthentication within two minutes.
Learn more →

Add custom HTTP headers in Microsoft Entra Internet Access | General Availability
Custom headers enable granular SaaS access control, enforcing tenant restrictions across services like GitHub and Slack at the network layer. TLS inspection remains required for HTTPS destinations.
Learn more →

Outcome: Reduce the cost and complexity of access management

Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication | General Availability
Organizations can now select supported providers (Soprano, Telesign, Infobip) for SMS and voice delivery while Entra continues managing authentication logic. Setup before February 1, 2027, when Microsoft-provided delivery retires.
Learn more →

Sync devices to Entra ID for hybrid join | General Availability
Entra Cloud Sync can now synchronize AD computer objects to Entra ID, enabling hybrid join. Admins simply enable device sync within Cloud Sync configuration.
Learn more →

Outcome: Adopt AI safely at enterprise scale

Automate lifecycle management of agent identities | Public Preview
Policy-based guardrails help ensure agent identities don’t outlive their purpose. Configure reconfirmation intervals, sponsor requirements, and inactivity monitoring. A default inactivity policy (available to all tenants, no license required) notifies owners after 60 days of inactivity and disables the identity if no new activity occurs.
Learn more →

Tell Us What You Think

We began organizing this series around customer outcomes last month. Is that making it easier to connect what we're shipping to the challenges you're working through? I'd welcome your feedback in the comments.


Onwards,
Yina Arenas
Corporate Vice President and Chief Product Officer, Microsoft Identity and Network Access
Follow me on LinkedIn

 

Catch Microsoft Entra at Ignite, November 17-20, 2026, in San Francisco and online. See the Entra session schedule and RSVP today.
